24	📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/01_cover.svg` (or "None (free design)")
25	🎯 **Adherence rules / layout strategy**: [specific description]
26	```
27	
28	- **Content pages**: Templates only define header and footer; the content area is freely laid out by the Executor
29	- **No template**: Generate entirely per the Design Specification & Content Outline
30	
31	---
32	
33	## 2. Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory Step)
34	
35	> Before generating the first SVG page, you **must review the key design parameters from the Design Specification & Content Outline** to ensure all subsequent generation strictly follows the spec.
36	
37	Must output confirmation including: canvas dimensions, body font size, color scheme (primary/secondary/accent HEX values), font plan.
38	
39	**Why is this step mandatory?** Prevents the "spec says one thing, execution does another" disconnect.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 3. Execution Guidelines
44	
45	- **Proximity principle**: Place related elements close together to form visual groups; increase spacing between unrelated groups to reinforce logical structure
46	- **Absolute spec adherence**: Strictly follow the color, layout, canvas format, and typography parameters in the spec
47	- **Follow template structure**: If templates exist, inherit the template's visual framework
48	- **Phased batch generation** (recommended):
49	  1. **Visual Construction Phase**: Generate all SVG pages continuously, ensuring high consistency in design style and layout coordinates (Visual Consistency)
50	  2. **Logic Construction Phase**: After all SVGs are finalized, batch-generate speaker notes to ensure narrative coherence (Narrative Continuity)
51	- **Technical specifications**: See [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md) for SVG technical constraints and PPT compatibility rules
52	
53	### SVG File Naming Convention
54	
55	File naming format: `<number>_<page_name>.svg`
56	
57	- **Chinese content** → Chinese naming: `01_封面.svg`, `02_目录.svg`, `03_核心优势.svg`
58	- **English content** → English naming: `01_cover.svg`, `02_agenda.svg`, `03_key_benefits.svg`
59	- **Number rules**: Two-digit numbers, starting from 01
60	- **Page name**: Concise and descriptive, matching the page title in the Design Specification & Content Outline
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 4. Icon Usage
65	
66	Four approaches: **A: Emoji** (`<text>🚀</text>`) | **B: AI-generated** (SVG basic shapes) | **C: Built-in library** (`templates/icons/` 640+ icons, recommended) | **D: Custom** (user-specified)
67	
68	**Built-in icons — Placeholder method (recommended)**:
69	
70	```xml
71	<use data-icon="chart-bar" x="100" y="200" width="48" height="48" fill="#005587"/>
72	```
73	
74	> No need to manually run `embed_icons.py`; `finalize_svg.py` post-processing tool will auto-embed icons.
75	
76	**Common icons**: `chart-bar` `arrow-trend-up` `users` `cog` `circle-checkmark` `target` `clock` `file` `dollar` `lightbulb`
77	
78	> ⚠️ **Icon validation rule**: If the Design Specification includes an icon inventory list, Executor may **only** use icons from that approved list. Using icon names not in the index is FORBIDDEN — verify against `templates/icons/icons_index.json` if uncertain.
79	
80	Full index: `templates/icons/README.md`
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 5. Chart Reference
85	
86	When the Design Spec includes a **VII. Chart Reference List**, read the referenced SVG templates from `templates/charts/` to understand common chart patterns.
87	
88	**Adaptation rules**:
89	- **Must preserve**: Chart type (bar/line/pie etc.) as specified in the Design Spec
90	- **Must adapt**: Data values, labels, colors (match the project's color scheme), and dimensions to fit the page layout
91	- **May adjust**: Axis ranges, grid lines, legend position, spacing — as long as the chart remains accurate and readable
92	- **Must NOT**: Change chart type without Design Spec justification, or remove data points specified in the outline
93	
94	> Chart templates: `templates/charts/` (33 types). Index: `templates/charts/charts_index.json`
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 6. Image Handling
99	
100	Handle images based on their status in the Design Specification's "Image Resource List":
101	
102	| Status | Source | Handling |
103	|--------|--------|----------|
104	| **Existing** | User-provided | Reference images directly from `../images/` directory |
105	| **AI-generated** | Generated by Image_Generator | Images already in `../images/`, reference directly |
106	| **Placeholder** | Not yet prepared | Use dashed border placeholder |
107	
108	**Reference**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" ... preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
109	
110	**Placeholder**: Dashed border `<rect stroke-dasharray="8,4" .../>` + description text
111	
112	---
113	
114	## 7. Font Usage
115	
116	Apply corresponding fonts for different text roles based on the font plan in the Design Specification & Content Outline:
117	
118	| Role | Chinese Recommended | English Recommended |
119	|------|--------------------|--------------------|
120	| Title font | Microsoft YaHei / KaiTi / SimHei | Arial / Georgia |
121	| Body font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Calibri / Times |
122	| Emphasis font | SimHei | Arial Black / Consolas |
123	| Annotation font | Microsoft YaHei / SimSun | Arial / Times |
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
128	
129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
130	
131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
132	
133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
134	
135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.
136	
137	**Basic stage direction markers** (common to all styles):
138	
139	| Marker | Purpose |
140	|--------|---------|
141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |
143	
144	> Each style may extend with additional markers (`[Interactive]`/`[Data]`/`[Scan Room]`/`[Benchmark]` etc.), see `executor-{style}.md`.
145	
146	**Requirements**:
147	
148	- Notes should be conversational and flow naturally
149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points
150	- Users can manually edit and override in the `notes/` directory
151	
152	### Task 2. Split Into Per-Page Note Files
153	
154	Automatically split `notes/total.md` into individual speaker note files in the `notes/` directory.
155	
156	**File naming convention**:
157	
158	- **Recommended**: Match SVG names (e.g., `01_cover.svg` → `notes/01_cover.md`)
159	- **Compatible**: Also supports `slide01.md` format (backward compatibility)
160	
161	---
162	
163	## 9. Next Steps After Completion
164	
165	> **Auto-continuation**: After Visual Construction Phase (all SVG pages) and Logic Construction Phase (all notes) are complete, the Executor proceeds directly to the post-processing pipeline.
166	
167	**Post-processing & Export** (see [shared-standards.md](shared-standards.md)):
168	
169	```bash
170	# 1. Split speaker notes
171	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
172	
173	# 2. SVG post-processing (auto-embed icons, images, etc.)
174	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
175	
176	# 3. Export PPTX
177	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
178	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
179	```

1	# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)
2	
3	> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Role Definition
8	
9	An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)
14	
15	Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:
16	
17	| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
18	|---------|---------|---------------|
19	| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
20	| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
21	| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
22	| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |
23	
24	**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S
25	
26	**Title writing**:
27	
28	| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
29	|-------------|------------|-----------------|
30	| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
31	| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
32	| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
33	| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)
38	
39	> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.
40	
41	| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
42	|--------|---------|----------------------|
43	| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
44	| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
45	| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
46	| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
47	| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |
48	
49	**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")
50	
51	```xml
52	<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
53	<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
54	<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
55	```
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)
60	
61	> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.
62	
63	```
64	         ┌─────────────────┐
65	         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
66	         └────────┬────────┘
67	      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
68	  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
69	  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
70	  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
71	```
72	
73	| Level | Position | Font Size |
74	|-------|----------|-----------|
75	| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
76	| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
77	| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |
78	
79	**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## MBB-level Layout Patterns
84	
85	### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)
86	
87	```
88	┌──────────────────────────────────┐
89	│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
90	├──────────────────────────────────┤
91	│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
92	├──────────────────────────────────┤
93	│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
94	│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
95	├──────────────────────────────────┤
96	│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
97	│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
98	├──────────────────────────────────┤
99	│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
100	└──────────────────────────────────┘
101	```
102	
103	### Strategic Roadmap
104	
105	Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:
106	
107	```
108	Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
109	x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
110	```
111	
112	### Benchmarking Matrix
113	
114	Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.
115	
116	### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)
117	
118	Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.
119	
120	---
121	
122	## Strategic Use of Color
123	
124	MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:
125	
126	| Purpose | Method |
127	|---------|--------|
128	| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
129	| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
130	| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
131	| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |
132	
133	**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.
134	
135	---
136	
137	## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix
138	
139	| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
140	|----------|-----------------|--------|
141	| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
142	| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
143	| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
144	| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
145	| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
146	| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |
147	
148	---
149	
150	## Speaker Notes Style
151	
152	### Narrative Tone
153	
154	Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.
155	
156	### Stage Direction Markers
157	
158	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
159	|--------|---------|---------|
160	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
161	| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
162	| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
163	| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
164	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |
165	
166	### Notes Writing Guidelines
167	
168	- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
169	- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
170	- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
171	- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
172	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`
173	
174	### Notes Example
175	
176	```markdown
177	# 03_strategic_path
178	
179	[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.
180	
181	We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]
182	
183	Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
184	[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]
185	
186	Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
187	Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.
188	
189	[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?
190	
191	Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
192	Duration: 3 minutes
193	Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement
199	
200	### Content Level
201	
202	- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
203	- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
204	- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
205	- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive
206	
207	### Visual Level
208	
209	- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
210	- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
211	- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
212	- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout
213	
214	### Notes Level
215	
216	- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
217	- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
218	- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
    <!-- 模板: 内容页 - Google 风格 -->

    <defs>
        <!-- 顶部四色渐变条 -->
        <linearGradient id="topGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#4285F4;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="33%" style="stop-color:#EA4335;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="66%" style="stop-color:#FBBC04;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#34A853;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
    </defs>

    <!-- 白色背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF" />

    <!-- 顶部四色渐变条 -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="6" fill="url(#topGradient)" />

    <!-- 页面标题 -->
    <text x="60" y="85" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="46" font-weight="700" fill="#1A237E">
        {{PAGE_TITLE}}
    </text>

    <!-- 蓝色标题下划线 -->
    <rect x="60" y="100" width="120" height="4" rx="2" fill="#4285F4" />

    <!-- 内容区域 - 灵活布局占位 -->
    <!-- 
        可使用的布局模式：
        - KPI 网格 (2×2 或 2×3)
        - 左文右图 / 左图右文
        - 三栏卡片
        - 四象限
        - 上下分区
        - Dashboard 风格
        - 列表 + 说明
    -->
    <rect x="60" y="130" width="1160" height="520" fill="none" stroke="#E8EAED" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="8,8" />
    <text x="640" y="380" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9AA0A6" font-size="18" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif">
        {{CONTENT_AREA}}
    </text>
    <text x="640" y="420" text-anchor="middle" fill="#9AA0A6" font-size="14" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif">
        (由 Executor 根据实际内容自由布局)
    </text>

    <!-- 常用设计元素参考 -->
    <!-- 
        KPI 卡片: <rect rx="16" stroke="#4285F4" stroke-width="3" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
        浅灰背景块: <rect rx="12" fill="#F8F9FA"/>
        品牌色圆点: <circle r="12" fill="#4285F4"/>
        分隔线: <line stroke="#E8EAED" stroke-width="1"/>
        数据数字: font-size="56" font-weight="700" fill="#4285F4"
        数据标签: font-size="16" font-weight="500" fill="#5F6368"
    -->

    <!-- 底部四色圆点装饰 -->
    <g transform="translate(640, 680)">
        <circle cx="-60" cy="0" r="6" fill="#4285F4" />
        <circle cx="-30" cy="0" r="6" fill="#EA4335" />
        <circle cx="0" cy="0" r="6" fill="#FBBC04" />
        <circle cx="30" cy="0" r="6" fill="#34A853" />
        <circle cx="60" cy="0" r="6" fill="#4285F4" />
    </g>

    <!-- 页码（可选） -->
    <text x="1220" y="695" text-anchor="end" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#9AA0A6">
        {{PAGE_NUM}}
    </text>

</svg>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1280 720">
    <!-- 模板: 封面页 - Google 风格 -->

    <defs>
        <!-- 背景渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="bgGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#E8F0FE;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="50%" style="stop-color:#FFFFFF;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#E8F5E9;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>

        <!-- 标题渐变 -->
        <linearGradient id="titleGradient" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
            <stop offset="0%" style="stop-color:#1A73E8;stop-opacity:1" />
            <stop offset="100%" style="stop-color:#0D47A1;stop-opacity:1" />
        </linearGradient>
    </defs>

    <!-- 背景 -->
    <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGradient)" />

    <!-- 装饰圆形 - 增加视觉层次 -->
    <circle cx="150" cy="150" r="120" fill="#4285F4" fill-opacity="0.08" />
    <circle cx="1130" cy="570" r="150" fill="#34A853" fill-opacity="0.08" />
    <rect x="900" y="80" width="180" height="180" rx="20" fill="#FBBC04" fill-opacity="0.06" transform="rotate(15 990 170)" />

    <!-- 左侧四色竖条 -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="10" height="180" fill="#4285F4" />
    <rect x="0" y="180" width="10" height="180" fill="#EA4335" />
    <rect x="0" y="360" width="10" height="180" fill="#FBBC04" />
    <rect x="0" y="540" width="10" height="180" fill="#34A853" />

    <!-- 中央内容卡片 -->
    <rect x="280" y="180" width="720" height="360" rx="24" fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#E8EAED" stroke-width="1" />

    <!-- 主标题 -->
    <text x="640" y="280" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="52" font-weight="700" fill="url(#titleGradient)" text-anchor="middle">
        {{TITLE}}
    </text>

    <!-- 副标题 -->
    <text x="640" y="335" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="500" fill="#5F6368" text-anchor="middle">
        {{SUBTITLE}}
    </text>

    <!-- 四色分隔线 -->
    <line x1="380" y1="380" x2="530" y2="380" stroke="#4285F4" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" />
    <line x1="550" y1="380" x2="620" y2="380" stroke="#EA4335" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" />
    <line x1="640" y1="380" x2="710" y2="380" stroke="#FBBC04" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" />
    <line x1="730" y1="380" x2="900" y2="380" stroke="#34A853" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" />

    <!-- 演讲者姓名 -->
    <text x="640" y="440" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="700" fill="#1A237E" text-anchor="middle">
        {{SPEAKER_NAME}}
    </text>

    <!-- 演讲者职位 -->
    <text x="640" y="478" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="400" fill="#5F6368" text-anchor="middle">
        {{SPEAKER_TITLE}}
    </text>

    <!-- 日期 -->
    <g transform="translate(640, 510)">
        <circle cx="0" cy="0" r="3" fill="#4285F4" />
        <text x="0" y="25" font-family="system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="500" fill="#5F6368" text-anchor="middle">
            {{DATE}}
        </text>
    </g>

    <!-- 底部四色圆点装饰 -->
    <circle cx="520" cy="630" r="12" fill="#4285F4" fill-opacity="0.9" />
    <circle cx="570" cy="630" r="10" fill="#EA4335" fill-opacity="0.9" />
    <circle cx="610" cy="630" r="14" fill="#FBBC04" fill-opacity="0.9" />
    <circle cx="660" cy="630" r="10" fill="#34A853" fill-opacity="0.9" />
    <circle cx="700" cy="630" r="12" fill="#4285F4" fill-opacity="0.9" />
    <circle cx="750" cy="630" r="10" fill="#EA4335" fill-opacity="0.9" />

</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

[Pause] Today, we present findings from Google's comprehensive survey of 1,001 real-world generative AI use cases across global enterprise customers.

[Data] 1,001 use cases | 11 industries | 6 agent types | 10× growth in 18 months

This deck is designed to equip enterprise leaders with a structured understanding of where gen AI is delivering measurable ROI today — organized by industry and agent type — so you can identify high-impact opportunities for your own organizations.

Key points: (1) 1,001 real-world production deployments (2) Organized by industry vertical and agent type (3) Data from Google Cloud customers as of October 2025
Duration: 1 minute

---
# 02_growth_trajectory

[Transition] Let's begin with the headline finding: the scale of enterprise gen AI adoption.

[Data] 101 → 1,001 use cases in 18 months — that's a 10× growth trajectory.

This growth curve reflects the acceleration of enterprise gen AI adoption from April 2024 (Cloud Next '24) to October 2025. What started as 101 use cases has grown into a comprehensive catalog of production deployments. The October 2025 edition added 400 new entries — and Google notes this still only scratches the surface.

[Benchmark] Compared to early pilot programs, today's deployments represent full production implementations at enterprise scale.

[Pause] The trajectory suggests we're still in the early exponential phase of gen AI adoption.

Key points: (1) 10× growth in 18 months — from 101 to 1,001 (2) April 2024 to October 2025 timeline (3) 400 new entries in latest update shows accelerating pace
Duration: 2 minutes

---
# 03_industry_agent_taxonomy

[Transition] To help you navigate this landscape, Google Cloud organized the 1,001 use cases into a taxonomy framework: 11 industries crossed with 6 agent types.

This matrix shows which combinations are most active. Green dots indicate active deployments; yellow shows emerging areas; gray indicates limited reported use.

[Scan Room] You can see that Customer and Employee agents dominate across most industries — this is where most organizations are starting.

The 6 agent types provide a structured framework for thinking about gen AI opportunities:
- **Customer Agents**: Conversational assistants handling external queries
- **Employee Agents**: Workplace productivity tools for internal use
- **Creative Agents**: Content generation at scale
- **Code Agents**: Developer productivity tools
- **Data Agents**: Analytics and data processing
- **Security Agents**: Threat detection and compliance

Key points: (1) 11 industry verticals × 6 agent types framework (2) Customer and Employee agents most common entry points (3) Matrix helps identify high-activity areas
Duration: 3 minutes

---
# 04_automotive_logistics

[Transition] Let's drill into one vertical as a representative example: Automotive & Logistics, which provides one of the richest cross-sections of agent types.

This table shows real deployments organized by agent type. Notice the breadth: Customer agents like Mercedes-Benz MBUX and GM OnStar, Employee agents like Toyota's factory AI platform and Uber's CS summarization, and Code agents like Renault Ampere.

[Data] LUXGEN reduced customer service workload by 30% using a Vertex AI chatbot.

[Data] Toyota saved 10,000+ man-hours per year with their factory AI platform.

[Data] PODS and Tombras generated 6,000+ unique ad headlines across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just 29 hours using Gemini.

[Pause] These aren't pilot programs — they're production results from real enterprise deployments.

Key points: (1) Rich cross-section of all agent types in Automotive & Logistics (2) Real company names, real use cases, real metrics (3) Production results, not pilots
Duration: 3 minutes

---
# 05_measurable_roi

[Transition] Speaking of production results — let's look at the quantified ROI being achieved.

[Data] Mercari anticipates 500% ROI while reducing employee workloads by 20% through AI-powered customer service.

[Data] LUXGEN achieved 30% customer service workload reduction with their Vertex AI chatbot.

[Data] Toyota's factory AI platform saved over 10,000 man-hours per year.

[Data] PODS generated 6,000+ unique ad headlines across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just 29 hours.

[Pause] These are production results — not theoretical projections or pilot metrics.

The key insight: measurable ROI is achievable within months, not years. Organizations that have deployed gen AI in production are seeing tangible business outcomes.

Key points: (1) 500% ROI achievable (2) 30% workload reduction common (3) 10,000+ hours saved annually (4) Production results, not pilots
Duration: 2 minutes

---
# 06_cross_industry_patterns

[Transition] When we look across all 1,001 use cases, three dominant patterns emerge.

**Pattern 1: Conversational Customer Agents** — the most visible entry point. Automotive companies like Mercedes-Benz, GM, and VW deploy AI-powered virtual assistants to handle customer queries, reduce wait times, and lower human agent workloads. Financial services like Commerzbank are doing the same.

**Pattern 2: Employee Productivity Agents** — the broadest category. Companies like Uber, Rivian, and Geotab use Gemini for Google Workspace to summarize documents, accelerate research, draft content, and filter data across departments.

**Pattern 3: Creative and Scale Agents** — the fastest-growing frontier. Virgin Voyages creates hyper-personalized video campaigns with Veo. PODS runs adaptive billboards. Figma generates brand-approved assets instantly. Gen AI is moving from text into multimodal creative production at enterprise scale.

[Pause] Notice the progression: most organizations start with customer agents, then move to employee productivity, then explore creative and code agents.

Key points: (1) Customer agents: most visible entry point (2) Employee agents: broadest category (3) Creative agents: fastest-growing frontier
Duration: 3 minutes

---
# 07_strategic_takeaways

[Transition] Let me leave you with five actionable takeaways for your gen AI strategy.

**1. Gen AI is production-ready across all major industries.** The 1,001 use cases represent real enterprise implementations, not experiments. Your peers are deploying gen AI in production today.

**2. Customer and Employee agents are the most common entry points.** Start here for quick wins. Conversational assistants deliver visible ROI within months through reduced wait times and lower human agent workloads.

**3. Measurable ROI is achievable within months.** 500% ROI (Mercari), 30% workload reduction (LUXGEN), 10,000+ man-hours saved annually (Toyota) — these are production results, not projections.

**4. Creative and Code agents are emerging fast.** The next wave of value is coming from multimodal creative production and developer productivity tools. Virgin Voyages, Figma, and Renault Ampere are early examples.

**5. The pace of adoption is accelerating.** With 400 new entries in the latest update alone, the trajectory suggests enterprise gen AI deployment is still in its early exponential phase. Early movers gain compounding advantages.

[Scan Room] I'm happy to discuss how these patterns might apply to your specific industry and use cases.

Key points: (1) Production-ready across 11 industries (2) Start with Customer/Employee agents (3) ROI achievable within months (4) Creative and Code agents emerging fast (5) Accelerating adoption — early movers win
Duration: 3 minutes
